newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish bond yields dip as crown recovers slightly.
newsitem.headline: Swedish bond yields dip as crown recovers slightly.

text.p: The Swedish crown lost ground during the day Tuesday but managed to regain some strength in late trade, triggering a fall in bond yields.
"We came up to some attractive levels at around 4.55/4.57 where buyers of the crown stepped in. We have seen buyers of crown all the way in this downward move," one dealer said.
The Riksbank left its key repo rate unchanged at 4.10 percent at its weekly tender which was as expected.
The National Debt Office lowered its forecast for the state borrowing need for 1997 to between zero-10 billion crowns from 10-20 billion but this only affected the market marginally.
The market focus was now on further announcements by the French Government and on German efforts to meet Maastricht criteria.
The six month T-bill rate fell four basis points to 4.20 percent and the ten year bond yield fell three basis points to 6.96 percent.
The crown softened to 4.5380 crowns to the mark compared to 4.5300 crowns in late trade on Monday.
